content: 1. 2. Binbay et al. (2010) reported a high prevalence of psychosis in urbanized areas of Turkey, as part of the TURSCH study, published in Schizophrenia Research. 3. Borders and Grobman (2007) investigated the relationship between chronic stress and low birth weight in neonates among low-income women, published in Obstetrics & Gynecology. 4. Chen and Deater-Deckard (2014) explored how temperament and family environment interactions influence child maladjustment, as published in the Journal of Abnormal Child Psychology. 5. Coutinho et al. (2014) examined the prevalence of common mental disorders and their relationship to social context in São Paulo, Brazil, using multilevel analysis, published in Cadernos de Saúde Pública. 6. Drury and Norheim (2006) reviewed housing space standards for the Greater London Authority but did not include original data. 7. Eriksson and Romelsjo (2011) conducted a 35-year longitudinal cohort study on early risk factors for criminal offending in individuals with schizophrenia, published in Social Psychiatry & Psychiatric Epidemiology. 8. 9. Ferguson and Cassells (2013) provided an international review of the physical environment's impact on child development, published in the International Journal of Psychology. 10. Fisher and Tran (2007) studied the relationship between socioeconomic advantage and mood during advanced pregnancy in Vietnamese women, published in the International Journal of Mental Health Systems. 11. Fisher and de Mello (2011) emphasized the importance of recognizing maternal mental health in resource-constrained settings to achieve Millennium Development Goals, as stated in the Ha Noi Expert Statement. 12. Gariepy and Blair (2014) analyzed neighborhood characteristics and their 10-year risk of depression in Canadian adults with and without chronic illness, published in Health & Place. 13. Grzywacz and Quandt (2010) examined depressive symptoms among Latino farmworkers across agricultural seasons, focusing on structural and situational influences, published in Cultural Diversity & Ethnic Minority Psychology. 14. Guite and Clark (2006) reviewed the impact of physical and urban environments on mental well-being, published in Public Health. 15. Handy (2014) provided an introduction to the relationship between housing, health, and social care, published in the Journal of Integrated Care. 16. 17. Hunter-Hernandez and Costas-Muniz (2014) studied the quality of life and household composition of Latino and Black cancer patients, published in Psycho-Oncology. 18. Kyle and Dunn (2008) reviewed the effects of housing circumstances on health, quality of life, and healthcare use for individuals with severe mental illness, published in Health & Social Care in the Community. 19. Lemery-Chalfant and Kao (2013) explored childhood temperament and its interaction with family environment, published in Development & Psychopathology. 20. The London Health Commission (2005) reviewed health indicators in London, focusing on children and young people, but did not include original data. 21. Mariu and Merry (2012) investigated mental health help-seeking behaviors among New Zealand secondary school students, published in Clinical Child Psychology & Psychiatry. 22. Maziak and Ward (2005) mapped health and environmental conditions in informal zones in Aleppo, Syria, based on the Aleppo Household Survey, published in the International Archives of Occupational & Environmental Health. 23. McNeely and Waldstein (2013) examined the impact of poor-quality residential environments on physical and mental health-related quality of life in urban adults, published in Psychosomatic Medicine. 24. Murphy (2013) conducted a longitudinal multilevel analysis on the impact of child maltreatment on behavioral outcomes, as part of a dissertation. 25. Ndom and Igbokwe (2012) studied overcrowding, age, and gender differences in state anxiety among Nigerian undergraduate students, published in IFE Psychologia. 26. Packard and Bezlyak (2011) found that early-life socioeconomic adversity is associated with chronic inflammation, carotid atherosclerosis, poorer lung function, and decreased cognitive performance in adulthood, published in BMC Public Health. 27. Pevalin and Taylor (2008) analyzed the dynamics of unhealthy housing in the UK using panel data, published in Housing Studies. 28. Rahi and Kumavat (2005) examined socio-demographic correlates of psychiatric disorders, published in the Indian Journal of Pediatrics. 29. Rice (2006) compared the lives of children across Britain’s housing divide, published by Shelter. 30. Rohe and Han (2012) called for renewed collaboration between housing and health sectors, published in the North Carolina Medical Journal. 31. Rollings (2014) assessed the influence of built and natural environments on mental and physical health, as part of a dissertation. 32. Sahin and Kilicarslan (2010) studied depressive and anxiety levels in third-trimester pregnant women, published in the Trakya University Medical Faculty Journal. 33. Sengupta and Osborne (2012) analyzed the relationship between income and subjective well-being in New Zealand, published in the New Zealand Journal of Psychology. 34. Jones et al. (2005) conducted a national investigation into the housing crisis in the UK, published by Shelter. 35. Shepherd and Li (2012) examined socioeconomic disparities in the mental health of Indigenous children in Western Australia, published in BMC Public Health. 36. 37. Suglia and Duarte (2011) studied the effects of housing quality and instability on maternal mental health, published in the Journal of Urban Health. 38. Williams and Kooner (2007) published an erratum in the British Journal of Health Psychology. 39. Yadav and Anita (2006) examined the effect of residential density on mental health, published in the Indian Journal of Community Psychology.
